 Oral Judgment

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act',
for short) has been filed by the Insurance Company being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 22.02.2018 NC: 2024:KHC:37649 passed by the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Nanjangud (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.1219/2015.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 19.11.2014 at about 2.30 p.m.,
when the deceased Somashekarmurthy was proceeding in a tempo bearing registration No.KA-09/7026 as a passenger, when they reached near the land of one Manikanta at Heggadahalli village, Nanjangud - Hullahalli road, at that time, the driver of the said vehicle drove the same at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, due to which the tempo toppled towards left.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 to 3 appeared through counsel and respondent No.3 filed NC: 2024:KHC:37649 written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The claimants, in order to prove the case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1,
and another witness as PW-2, and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 and C1.
On behalf of respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R2.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia

, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.9,54,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.

The learned counsel for the Insurance Company raised the following contentions:
i) Firstly, as on the date of the accident the offending vehicle was not having a valid permit and fitness certificate.

Since the insured has violated the policy condition,
Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation ii) Secondly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation aw by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Hence, sought to allow the appeal.
7. None appears for the respondents.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and the original records.
9.
It is not in dispute that Somashekaramurthy died in the road traffic accident occurred on 19.11.2014 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

sentences.text: The only ground urged by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company is that, as on the date of the accident the offending vehicle was not having a valid permit and fitness certificate.

The Tribunal has considered this aspect of the matter and after considering the judgment of this Court in the case of RANGAPPA @ RANGAPPA SHETTY vs. JAYARAMAIAH AND ANOTHER reported in ILR 2014 Kar.191, has held that not possessing of fitness certificate as on the date of the accident will not exonerate the Insurance Company from the liability.

sentences.text: In the subsequent judgment of this Court in the case of SHIVANNA B.K. vs. SHIVAMMA N.J. & OTHERS (MFA No.7387/2015 disposed of on 18.02.2020), it is held that unless registration certificate is cancelled on the ground of not having fitness certificate, the Insurance Company cannot be exonerated.

11. In respect of quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal, after considering the age and NC: 2024:KHC:37649 avocation of the deceased, granted a just and reasonable compensation.
12. Hence, the appeal is dismissed.
The amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
